name: async-multiple

Combobox.Value: children (render prop receiving the selected value array)

whatItDemonstrates: Multiple-select combobox that fetches people from a simulated remote search on input changes, keeps already-selected users merged into the items list, and renders selections as removable chips with async status/empty/error messaging.
stateManaged: uncontrolled with app-side mirrors — Root value and inputValue are not controlled; selectedValues/searchValue/error/blockStartStatus useState plus a selectedValuesRef are updated via onValueChange/onInputValueChange only to derive the memoized items merge and status UI, with useTransition tracking fetch pending state
nonTrivialInteractions: External filtering: filter={null} disables the internal filter; Combobox.useFilter().contains is passed into a simulated searchUsers fetch matching name/username/email/title
Abortable fetches: each non-empty input change creates an AbortController, aborts the previous one, and results are applied only if not aborted (inside startTransition)
onInputValueChange skips fetching for empty input (results reset to the selected users) and for reason === 'item-press'
items is a useMemo merging searchResults with all selectedValues so selected users stay selectable after result windows change
onOpenChangeComplete on close resets searchResults to the selected users and clears blockStartStatus
onValueChange updates a ref+state mirror, clears the query/error, and toggles blockStartStatus to suppress the 'Start typing' status after a selection
Status area renders a spinner while pending, the fetch error, 'Start typing to search people…', or 'No matches for "…"'; Empty renders 'Try a different search term.'
Chips with aria-label/aria-description, ChipRemove aria-label, and Input aria-description describing Left-Arrow chip navigation; placeholder is empty once selections exist
Popup aria-busy reflects pending fetches

name: async-single
whatItDemonstrates: Single-select combobox that searches a simulated remote directory on input changes with abortable fetches, transition-driven pending state, and status/empty messaging while keeping the selected user in the items list.
stateManaged: uncontrolled with app-side mirrors — Root value and inputValue are not controlled; selectedValue/searchValue/error useState are updated via onValueChange/onInputValueChange to derive the memoized items merge and status text, with useTransition tracking fetch pending state
nonTrivialInteractions: External filtering: filter={null} disables the internal filter; Combobox.useFilter().contains is passed into a simulated searchUsers fetch matching name/username/email/title
Abortable fetches: each non-empty, non-item-press input change creates an AbortController, aborts the previous one, and applies results only if not aborted (inside startTransition)
onInputValueChange resets results/error on empty input and skips fetching when reason === 'item-press'
items is a useMemo appending selectedValue to searchResults when absent so the selection stays available
onOpenChangeComplete on close (when a value is selected) narrows results to [selectedValue]
Status area renders a spinner while pending, the fetch error, 'Start typing to search people…', or 'No matches for "…"'; Empty renders 'Try a different search term.'
Popup aria-busy reflects pending fetches; inline input with Clear and Trigger buttons in the InputGroup
discrepancies: Variant divergence (not styling): the tailwind variant creates/assigns the AbortController after the empty-input and 'item-press' early returns, so those changes do not abort an in-flight search; the css-modules variant creates the controller before those early returns, so empty-input and item-press changes also abort pending fetches.

name: creatable

Combobox.Value: children (render prop receiving the selected value array)
Combobox.List: children (render prop branching on the creatable marker)
Combobox.Item: value (the item object, including the synthetic creatable item)

whatItDemonstrates: Multiple-select label picker where a non-matching query surfaces a synthetic 'Create "…"' item that opens a creation Dialog (with confirm/cancel) to add and select the new label.
stateManaged: controlled — Root value={selected} and inputValue={query} each wrapped in useState; plus labels list state, openDialog state, and refs for the pending query, highlighted item, dialog input, and combobox input
nonTrivialInteractions: itemsForView appends a synthetic { creatable, id: 'create:…', value: 'Create "…"' } item whenever the trimmed query is non-empty and no exact case-insensitive match exists
onValueChange intercepts selection of the creatable item: it stashes the query in pendingQueryRef and opens the Dialog instead of selecting; normal selections filter out creatable rows
Custom Enter handling on Combobox.Input (onKeyDown): with no highlighted item, selects the existing case-insensitive match or opens the creation Dialog
onItemHighlighted records the highlighted item in a ref to gate the Enter-to-create behavior
handleCreate reads the dialog input (falling back to the combobox input), dedupes case-insensitively, and generates collision-free ids before adding to labels and selection
Controlled Dialog with initialFocus on the create input, form submit to create, Dialog.Close to cancel; query reset on both paths
Chips with aria-label/aria-description and ChipRemove aria-label, mirroring the multiple-select chip pattern

name: create-items

Combobox.Item: value (the derived ID from the collection)

whatItDemonstrates: Single-select combobox over a module-scope Combobox.createItems(fruits, { getValue, getLabel }) collection where selection uses derived IDs (defaultValue='banana') while the list renders labels.
stateManaged: uncontrolled — defaultValue='banana' (a derived ID); no app state
nonTrivialInteractions: Combobox.createItems derives selection values (fruit.id) and display labels (fruit.name) from raw records at module scope
Combobox.Item receives value={item.id} (the derived ID) rather than the rendered item, and the List render prop displays item.name
defaultValue selects by derived ID; default collator filtering runs against the derived labels
Inline input with Clear and Trigger buttons in the InputGroup; Empty message when nothing matches

name: grouped

Combobox.Root: items (grouped shape: array of { value, items })
Combobox.Collection: children (render prop per item within the group)

whatItDemonstrates: Filterable single-select combobox whose items are grouped into 'Fruits' and 'Vegetables' sections with GroupLabel headings rendered via Group/Collection.
stateManaged: none — fully uncontrolled (no value/defaultValue, no app state); grouping is computed at module scope by groupProduce()
nonTrivialInteractions: Grouped items data shape: array of { value (heading text), items: Produce[] } objects built at module scope with fixed group order

Combobox.List render prop receives each group; Combobox.Group re-scopes filtering/registration with its items prop and renders a GroupLabel heading plus a Combobox.Collection render prop for the per-group Item rows
Default collator filtering operates across the grouped structure; Empty message when nothing matches
Inline input with Clear and Trigger buttons in the InputGroup

name: hero
whatItDemonstrates: Baseline single-select filterable combobox over a flat fruit list with an inline input, clear and trigger buttons inside the InputGroup, an empty state, and check-mark item indicators.
stateManaged: none — fully uncontrolled (no value/defaultValue, no app state)
nonTrivialInteractions: Native <label htmlFor={id}> wired to Combobox.Input via React.useId for the accessible name
Default collator filtering over item labels; Combobox.Item receives the item object itself as value
Combobox.Clear (X icon) clears the selection and Combobox.Trigger (caret icon) opens the popup, both with aria-labels
Combobox.Empty renders 'No fruits found.'; ItemIndicator shows a check mark on the selected item
Popup anchored to the input with sideOffset and styled with --anchor-width/--available-width/transform-origin CSS vars

name: input-inside-popup
whatItDemonstrates: Searchable select pattern where the trigger is a button labeled by Combobox.Label (showing Combobox.Value with placeholder and an Icon) and the filter input is rendered inside the popup above the list.
stateManaged: none — fully uncontrolled (no value/defaultValue, no app state)
nonTrivialInteractions: Input-inside-popup composition: Combobox.Input is the first child of Combobox.Popup rather than an inline field; the trigger opens the popup for filtering
Combobox.Label provides the visible label for the trigger (the form control in this pattern)
Combobox.Value renders the placeholder 'Select country' when nothing is selected; Combobox.Icon renders a caret-up/down glyph inside the trigger
Popup carries aria-label='Select country'; list area height is budgeted via a --input-container-height CSS var so the input stays visible
Default collator filtering over ~200 country objects; Empty message when nothing matches
Positioner uses align='start'

name: multiple

Combobox.Value: children (render prop receiving the selected value array)

whatItDemonstrates: Multiple-select combobox rendering selections as removable chips inside the input, with screen-reader hints for chip removal and Left-Arrow chip navigation.
stateManaged: none — fully uncontrolled (no value/defaultValue, no app state)
nonTrivialInteractions: Combobox.Value render prop maps selected values to Chips > Chip > ChipRemove; chips render inline in the InputGroup

Screen-reader attributes: Chips aria-label ('Selected languages' when non-empty), Chip aria-label/aria-description ('Press Backspace or Delete to remove'), ChipRemove aria-label ('Remove X'), Input aria-description describing Left-Arrow chip navigation
Input placeholder is 'e.g. TypeScript' only while nothing is selected, empty otherwise
Default collator filtering over the language list; Empty message when nothing matches
Item styling keys off data-selected (not just data-highlighted) to mark selected rows

name: virtualized

Combobox.List: children (static child, not a render prop)

whatItDemonstrates: Combobox over 10,000 items virtualized with @tanstack/react-virtual, using Combobox.useFilteredItems inside the list child and onItemHighlighted to keep highlight and scroll position in sync.
stateManaged: open state only, and it diverges by variant — tailwind controls it (useState open/onOpenChange, enabling the virtualizer only while open via enabled: open); css-modules leaves open uncontrolled and the virtualizer always enabled; no selection state in either variant
nonTrivialInteractions: Root has virtualized set; items come from a filtered window read via Combobox.useFilteredItems<VirtualizedItem>() inside the child rendered as a static child of Combobox.List
useVirtualizer drives absolutely-positioned Item rows (height/translateY from virtual item metrics) inside a total-size spacer div whose height feeds a --total-size CSS var on the scroller
Each virtualized Item gets index={virtualItem.index}, ref={virtualizer.measureElement}, aria-setsize, and aria-posinset for virtualized listbox semantics

onItemHighlighted syncs scrolling: reason 'none' or keyboard movement hitting the first/last index queues a queueMicrotask scrollToIndex (align 'start' at the end, 'end' otherwise) through a virtualizerRef exposed with useImperativeHandle
Scroll element is captured via a ref callback that also calls virtualizer.measure(); VirtualizedList renders null when no items match so Combobox.Empty shows 'No items found.'
itemToStringLabel maps items to their name for input value/typeahead
discrepancies: Variant divergence (not styling): the tailwind variant controls the popup open state (useState open + onOpenChange={setOpen}) and passes open to VirtualizedList, enabling the virtualizer only while open (enabled: open in useVirtualizer); the css-modules variant does not control open and enables the virtualizer unconditionally.
